summary: The agents roster follows this node's own writes within about one fold. A claim this node commits now cuts the refresher's pause to its floor (100 ms, or as long as the last fold took), the way a read waiting for a fresh roster already did. Before, the refresher folded on a fixed one-second pace, so a write waited up to a second plus a fold to appear in the published roster. That was most of the 'publish agents' latency on a busy host. Commits that hold only replicated claims keep the one-second pace.

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay change.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or migrations.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, registry or coordinated member upgrade change.

compatibility.detail: Readers, the published roster and its cuts are unchanged; only how soon a refresh follows a local commit changes.

downtime.detail: Takes effect on the next daemon start.

manual.detail: To see it, read the 'publish agents' path of /v1/client/request-latency (projection-fresh) after the roll. Its median and p99 should drop from about a second to about one fold. The refresher still pauses at least as long as each fold took, so it stays under about half a core.

recovery.detail: Rolling back restores the fixed one-second pace.
